Love the transparency in being able to see each user's voting habits. For me, this information helps in identifying accounts to follow/friend or ignore/hide. Perhaps this site could consider adopting some of the better RES features. I'd personally like to be able to auto-hide accounts that seem to be really spammy, trolly or astro-turfy. Maybe via that sort of transparency, this site can just let users police themselves. There are certainly pros/cons, but these are just ideas.

Joe_Bloe never contributes content, never upvotes but has a bajillion downvotes? Pretty obvious Troll account. Frank_the_Tank never upvotes or downvotes, but has 3000 submissions in the same type of content? Possibly astroturf marketing or serial reposter. A good balance of a ton of well-received content, a lot of upvotes and a few downvotes? Probably a good sign of a power user. I wonder if there are good metrics to weigh this stuff...but I suppose the more transparent the site is about its policies, that will increasingly tip-off anyone who would like to circumvent it.

This is probably a bad idea, but perhaps we could refine it: If things get out of hand, start an user-driven subverse that creates lists of accounts that seem to violate certain criteria, so people can make their own calls on blocking/friending. That's a ripe area for abuse, but it's more transparent if it's in the hands of the users and not that questionably-motivated shadowbanning b.s. by site admins.
1. Ability to auto-hide certain accounts. 2. An user-driven subverse that contains lists of accounts that seem to match certain criteria, so people can make their own calls on blocking/friending.
